direct_source_contracts.fact: Captures int(real time)+1 before inserting/cancelling the first job and before POST /api/notifications/email/test, then reuses this same explicit time for the ambiguous-send tick.
The real test-email endpoint persists due_at and created_at from a fresh wall-clock reading at enqueue time.
An explicit now is deliberately fixed; both pending selection and transactional claim require due_at <= that fixed value.
If a claimed provider call raises the injected TimeoutError, the normal caught-exception path records uncertain; the CI trace does not show that provider was reached.

independent_failure_analysis.proven_conditional_behavior: If the HTTP enqueue wall-clock time exceeds the earlier fixed now, the new test job is in the future for that tick and is correctly not claimed or sent. The test then cannot observe uncertain from that unattempted job.
ci_specific_unknowns: Original captured now value was not recorded.
New test job due_at/state/pref and provider invocation count were not recorded.
Whole-call duration does not identify the duration of the interval between initial now capture and HTTP enqueue.
The available report cannot uniquely prove wall-clock crossing as the historical CI failure cause.
independent_failure_analysis.recommendation: If authorized, use one module-scoped deterministic mail clock or drive the test from the actual persisted due_at; retain future-job exclusion, actual POST, provider-call assertion, uncertain non-replay and contact-revocation assertions. Do not alter production due-time policy or mark CI64 as passed.
